title: Food-system risk is being reframed as a governance problem spanning affordability, power, technology, health, and agency
source_unit: FAO Committee on World Food Security HLPE-FSN Note on Critical, Emerging and Enduring Issues for Food Security and Nutrition, launched 14 September 2026
geography: Global food-security and nutrition system foresight for the CFS strategic and multiyear policy agenda

observations.period: September 2026; critical, emerging, and enduring issue map

denominator.unit: critical, emerging, and enduring issues identified in the HLPE-FSN note

issue_frame.value: the note maps interconnections among food-system transformation, climate crises, geopolitical uncertainty and polycrises, international trade, corporate concentration, digital innovation and AI, One Health, healthy-diet affordability, and agency

policy_use.value: the note is intended to provide an evidence base for strategic discussions and the CFS multiyear programme of work

governance_context.value: persistent power imbalances and fragmented governance continue to shape food-security and nutrition outcomes

observations.method: The HLPE-FSN note provides a global foresight and issue-mapping synthesis for the Committee on World Food Security.
observations.uncertainty: An issue map identifies domains and interconnections but does not quantify the relative contribution of each issue or establish a common causal model.
observations.subgroup: Food producers, workers, consumers, communities, governments, international institutions, firms, civil society, and populations facing food insecurity or nutrition inequity.
observations.counterinterpretation: A broad systems map can support coordination while making prioritization and accountability harder if the links are not translated into specific decisions.

denominator.unit: HLPE-FSN food-system performance and nutrition frame

healthy_diet_cost.value: the cost of a healthy diet is positioned as a central food-system performance issue

hunger_context.value: global hunger is declining too slowly and healthy diets remain out of reach for billions

measurement_signal.value: the cost of a healthy diet is proposed as one of the clearest measures of whether food systems deliver what people need, not only calories

observations.method: The note connects food-system performance to affordability and dietary quality rather than aggregate calorie availability alone.
observations.uncertainty: The note's framing does not provide a new household-level affordability estimate, local price pass-through, or causal diet transition analysis.
observations.subgroup: Low-income households, children, women, older people, people with health conditions, food workers, and communities with limited access to diverse foods.
observations.counterinterpretation: Healthy-diet cost is important but cannot alone capture cultural preference, time, cooking infrastructure, food safety, or household agency.

observations.period: September 2026; power, market, and technology route

power.value: persistent power imbalances and corporate concentration are included among the food-system issues requiring attention

technology.value: digital innovation and artificial intelligence are included as forces reshaping food systems

trade.value: international trade and geopolitical uncertainty are treated as linked food-system pressures

observations.method: The note places markets, concentration, technology, trade, and geopolitics inside one food-system governance analysis.
observations.uncertainty: The framework does not measure market concentration, AI adoption, trade exposure, or bargaining power for every commodity or region.
observations.subgroup: Small producers, agricultural workers, food firms, retailers, consumers, regulators, digitally mediated food actors, and import-dependent economies.
observations.counterinterpretation: Technology and scale can improve efficiency or access, while concentration and digitalization can also deepen dependency, opacity, and unequal bargaining power.

observations.period: September 2026; health, resilience, and agency route

one_health.value: One Health is identified as a critical food-system issue

agency.value: agency is identified as an issue shaping food-security and nutrition futures

resilience.value: the note is intended to support strategic choices under climate, geopolitical, technological, and governance uncertainty

observations.method: The note integrates human, animal, environmental, institutional, and agency dimensions into a food-security and nutrition foresight frame.
observations.uncertainty: Including agency and One Health in the issue map does not measure participation, behavior, health outcomes, or resilience in specific populations.
observations.subgroup: Households, farmers, consumers, communities, health and environmental systems, food authorities, and groups with limited voice in food-system decisions.
observations.counterinterpretation: An integrated frame may reveal connections, but it can also dilute the visibility of concrete household choices, cultural food practices, and local accountability.

related_sources.claim: Complementary FAO flagship evidence on the high cost of healthy diets and global nutrition.
Complementary FAO commodity-market and food-supply monitoring.

boundary: This record adds a food-governance and agency route linking healthy-diet affordability, power, corporate concentration, trade, geopolitical uncertainty, digital and AI change, One Health, and participation. It uses a global foresight issue map, not household purchase histories, dietary intake records, market-concentration estimates for every commodity, causal nutrition effects, representative agency measures, or proof of policy implementation.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: FAO's official HLPE-FSN note announcement was reviewed for the ten-issue architecture, healthy-diet affordability framing, power and concentration, trade and geopolitical uncertainty, digital and AI change, One Health, agency, and CFS policy use.
